mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered 17.7 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w, signaling resumption of office commuting. This sustained workplace return over the next four weeks will drive weekday retail foot traffic as workers resume shopping routines adjacent to work locations, increasing RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -58.1 to -40.3 over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES declines below -45 in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has recovered 11.6 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w, indicating public transport confidence is returning. Increased transit use enables retail access for non-car users, directly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through expanded customer reach.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -65.7 to -54.1 over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or TRANSIT declines below -60 in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near -9.3 percent, indicating outdoor activity constraints remain binding. If PARKS mobility fails to improve beyond -5 percent within two weeks, consumers will redirect discretionary spending from outdoor recreation to indoor retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -5 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -9.3 in t-0w, showing minimal recovery
failure_condition: PARKS improves to above -5 percent within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline when PARKS constraint persists.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has improved 5.2 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w, signaling consumer confidence in essential shopping. This confidence spillover will increase discretionary retail visits as consumers perceive lower infection risk in commercial spaces, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -10.1 to -4.9 over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM remains above -3 percent, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts below -8 percent.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 27.1 to 20.9 percent over two weeks, indicating policy restrictions on stay-at-home orders are easing. failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not fall below 22 percent within one week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase when RESIDENTIAL is below 22 percent.

The joint improvement signals coordinated reopening of work and transport infrastructure. This interaction effect will compound retail recovery as commuting workers access retail during transit and work hours, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by >10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES +17.7 and TRANSIT +11.6 from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT declines below -50 percent in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS mobility show divergent trends: grocery confidence rising while parks remain constrained. This divergence indicates consumers are shifting from outdoor to indoor commercial activity. The substitution effect will increase RETAIL_REC as indoor retail becomes the primary discretionary destination over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves above -5 percent while PARKS remains below -8 percent
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -4.9 and PARKS at -9.3 in t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS improves above -5 percent before RETAIL_REC increases, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts below -8 percent, or RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks.
